holidays.name: International Yoga Day
holidays.description: Millions of people around the globe unroll their mats and strike a pose, from crowded city parks to quiet mountaintops, all in celebration of the ancient practice of yoga.
holidays.origin: Proposed by India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the UN General Assembly in 2014. The UN adopted the resolution that December, and the first celebration took place in 2015.
holidays.funFact: The first International Yoga Day set a Guinness World Record for the largest yoga session, with over 35,000 people participating in New Delhi.

holidays.name: World Humanist Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating reason, compassion, and human dignity, with humanists around the world marking the occasion with community events and good deeds.
holidays.origin: Established by the American Humanist Association in the 1980s and observed on the June solstice, linking the celebration of human values to the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.
holidays.funFact: It is celebrated on the solstice because humanists wanted a date tied to the natural world rather than to any religious calendar.

holidays.name: Go Skateboarding Day
holidays.description: Skaters everywhere hit the streets, parks, and ramps to roll, grind, and kickflip in honor of the sport, with the aim of getting more people on boards.
holidays.origin: Created in 2004 by the International Association of Skateboard Companies to promote skateboarding and to encourage cities to build more skateparks.
holidays.funFact: The holiday was created in part to push back against skateboarding bans, and it is now celebrated in dozens of countries around the world.

holidays.name: World Music Day (Fête de la Musique)
holidays.description: A giant free music party in which amateur and professional musicians perform in streets, plazas, and parks, so the whole city becomes a stage.
holidays.origin: Started in France in 1982 by Culture Minister Jack Lang and Maurice Fleuret, who wanted people to make music themselves rather than just listen. It has since spread to more than 120 countries.
holidays.funFact: The concept was inspired by an American musician, Joel Cohen, who proposed a similar all-night music festival on the solstice in 1976 on French radio.

holidays.name: Look Up at the Sky Day
holidays.description: A gentle invitation to stop staring at your screen and spend a few moments gazing at the clouds, the sun, and the sky above, especially fitting on the longest day of the year.
holidays.origin: An informal, unofficial observance that has circulated in holiday calendars, tied to the summer solstice and the idea of taking a mindful pause.
holidays.funFact: The June solstice happens when the Earth's axial tilt points the Northern Hemisphere closest to the sun, which gives places like Iceland and northern Norway near-endless daylight.
